newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namco raises C$20.8 mln for diamond mining.
newsitem.headline: Namco raises C$20.8 mln for diamond mining.

text.p: Canadian-listed Namibian Minerals Corporation Ltd said on Thursday it has issued 3.9 million shares to raise C$20.8 million to fund diamond mining and exploration activities in Namibia and Angola.
Namco chief executive officer Alastair Holberton said in a statement that several institutions had supported the share offer.
"Their participation is recognition of the growth prospects of the marine diamond mining industry and of Namibia's attractiveness as a prime emerging market," Holberton said.
The lead underwriter for the international syndication was Nomura International. Namco is listed on both the U.S.'s Nasdaq and Canadian stock exchanges in Toronto and Vancouver.

Namco is set to commission production from its Luderitz Bay grant with a target diamond output of 150,000 carats a year. The grant has a 2.6 million carat resource of gem quality diamonds valued at US$200 a carat.
Namibia's diamonds are 95 percent gem and are among the highest quality in the world.
Namco has so far raised C$73.9 million, mainly for investment in Namibia. It recently expanded into Angola to develop highly prospective diamond concessions.
It has 37.5 million shares in issue and a market capitalisation of C$225.3 million.
